scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Kuthiyottam is rooted in the ancient traditions of Kerala, specifically associated with the worship of the warrior goddess Bhadrakali.
Scholars have theorized that the ritual evolved from 'mock human sacrifice' practices that existed in the region's early history.
The dance serves as a living reenactment of the goddess's mythological battles, where the young performers represent her loyal, battle-worn soldiers.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: The ritual takes place during the annual Pongala festivals.
It is a form of spiritual offering where the physical suffering and discipline of the boys are seen as a sacrifice to the goddess.
The piercing and subsequent blood are symbolic of the wounds sustained by the goddess's army.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: The dance is characterized by highly energetic, synchronized movements performed by a group of boys.
Under the direction of an asan (conductor), the performers execute steps that are paced to the rapid beat of traditional drums.
The boys act as both dancers and singers, chanting rhythmic verses while moving.
Watch for Ritual Piercing.

scenes.title: Listen
narration: The primary musical accompaniment is provided by traditional Kerala drums, which dictate the tempo and energy of the performance.
The dancers themselves provide the vocal component, singing songs that are synchronized with the legends of the goddess.
Listen for the Drums.

The soundscape is dominated by the loud, rhythmic pulse of traditional drums, overlaid with the collective chanting of the young dancers. The music is designed to be driving and high-energy to match the physical intensity of the ritual.

scenes.title: The costume and the setting
narration: During the preparation phase, boys wear simple ascetic clothes.
For the final performance, they change into elaborate ceremonial costumes.
This often includes traditional headgear, waistbands, and ornaments.

scenes.title: The people
narration: The 'asan' is the central figure in Kuthiyottam, serving as the conductor, teacher, and spiritual guide for the young boys.
The asan is responsible for training the volunteers in the songs, steps, and the strict ascetic codes required for the ritual.
Variants of the dance and its associated piercing rituals are found in the Bhadrakali temples of the Alappuzha, Kollam, and Thiruvananthapuram districts.
The dance is passed down through temple-affiliated troupes and families.

scenes.title: A respectful note
narration: Kuthiyottam is a sacred ritual involving asceticism and symbolic sacrifice. Outsiders should observe with extreme respect, avoid interfering with the procession, and be aware that the ritual involves physical piercing which may be distressing to some viewers.
